newsitem.title: UK: LME copper ticks higher in late trading.
newsitem.headline: LME copper ticks higher in late trading.

text.p: LME copper retested the upside in late inter-office trading on Tuesday evening but failed to attain the $2,500 mark.
At 1800 GMT, three months copper was indicated at $2,490/94 per tonne, up from a kerb close of $2,479.
Sentiment took a knock, with talk that China may be a seller helping to unnerve the market and a strike at Inco providing only modest support, traders said.
Chartists said a second subsequent close below the 10-day moving average of $2,511 was a negative signal.
Nearby support was pegged at $2,470/75, based on Tuesday's and Monday's lows, followed by $2,440. Resistance was seen at $2,500 and $2,531.
Aluminium moved up a shade in sympathy, indicated at $1,580/82 compared to a $1,578 kerb close.
Zinc was at $1,335/37, up slightly from $1,334.
